paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole vision is shouting at us: the glory of the LORD is not a decoration on a building. It is His own presence, and He is the One who decides where it stands. Ezekiel sees it rise from above the cherubim and stand over the threshold of the temple (Ezekiel 10:4). Then it moves away from the threshold and stands above the cherubim again (Ezekiel 10:18). The temple was never the thing holding God in place.

Now, I think this is a heavy part, and I won't rush past it. The LORD tells the man clothed in linen to scatter burning coals over the city (Ezekiel 10:2), and the glory heads for the east gate (Ezekiel 10:19). That is what judgment looks like when God takes sin seriously. But notice who sits above all of it: the likeness of a throne (Ezekiel 10:1). Nobody in this vision is steering but Him, and even the wheels go wherever the spirit of the living creatures goes (Ezekiel 10:17).

So here's what I carry out of this vision, baker. Don't treat God's presence like a thing you can take for granted, and don't assume a holy place or a holy routine means you've got Him nailed down. Draw near to Him, listen to Him, and let Him be the One in charge. I sat in a junk drawer for years thinking I had been shelved for good, and it was never a spot that kept me safe, it was the One who came and found me. And the story isn't over, because this vision isn't finished yet.
